title: Annotatio II §.II: Adversaries pin crassior on Luther — Carlstadt’s Gott im Brod
pass_a_gloss: His Adversaries contend that Luther, after he rejected Transubstantiation, taught this [crasser mode] conceived either way. Carlstadt charges the former mode on Luther, addressing him thus: You will not long persuade me that God is in the bread? Likewise: How can one bring Christ into bread and wine?
pass_b_english: Adversaries say Luther taught that crasser mode after he rejected Transubstantiation.
Carlstadt pins local enclosure on him: You will not long persuade me that God is in the bread — and How can one bring Christ into bread and wine?
source_text: Hanc, utroque modo conceptam, à Luthero, post rejectam ab eo Transsubstantiationem, edoctam contendunt ejus Adversarii. Carlstadius, priorem modum Luthero impingit, ipsummet ita allocutus: Du wirst mich lang nicht überreden daß GOtt im Brod sey? Item: Wie kan man Christum ins Brod und Wein bringen?
